suite_command: npm test   (node --test; the run's own regression command at test, system-test and release-verify; 12 tests: paginate, TC_1-TC_4, ST_1 npm start smoke, GET /users/:id, strings, users)
baseline_summary: tests 12, pass 12, fail 0 on the unchanged copy (baseline.out in scratch); matches the run's own 12-test record at release-verify
method_notes: conditions.json was written from requirements.json alone before any file in repo or run_dir was opened.

The run's source and tests were read after that, before the variants were written; witnesses do not reuse the run's tests and start the product with `node src/server.js` on ports 41500-41599 (set via PORT). The run's own suite uses OS-assigned ephemeral ports (listen(0)), so no port range applied to it.

Primary variant per condition = the natural single-point implementation bug for that condition. Where a condition also names a status (R-1.7, R-2.13) or a header and a body (R-3.17), further variants for the other aspect were run and are listed in other_variants. `verdict` and `counts` follow the primary variant only; `counts_any_variant` counts a condition as survived if any of its variants passed the suite.

Every witness exits 0 on the unchanged copy and non-zero on every variant it was paired with (primary and other), each for the intended reason (witness message recorded in the scratch variant_results.json). No unrelated test (GET /users/:id, users, strings) failed under any variant, so no kill is a side effect of a broken variant.
The copy was restored after every variant; the full suite passed on the restored copy after every fifth condition and at the end (exit 0).

conditions.why_survived: Absent. R-3's 'Confirm by' list (invalid strings, fractional, zero, negatives, empty, size 101, valid boundaries) leaves out duplicates, and TC_3's oracle follows that list.
